# dsh-mermaid-panel
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness client plugin that adds a **Mermaid** page to the right Sidebar. It renders the M
ermaid diagrams in the conversation you are reading, without touching the conversation itself.

> Published as `dsh-mermaid-panel`, not `dsh-mermaid`: that package name belongs to
> MrmoLabs/dsh-m

ermaid, which renders
> diagrams inline in the chat instead. The two do different things and can be
> installed side by side.
## What it does
- Registers one right-Sidebar page type (`mermaid`) and a guide capsule, so the empty Sidebar offers

it as a door.
- Scans the rendered conversation for code blocks whose first line declares a Mermaid

diagram, and renders them in the page's own React tree.
- Each card keeps the authored source one c

lick away, plus copy.
- The card shows the diagram fitted and whole. Click the diagram, or **Enlarge

**, to open the full-screen view. Zoom and pan live there, not on the card.
- Re-renders when the pa
lette changes; the Sidebar's own docking, splitting, and per-Session tab persistence apply unchanged
ette changes; the Sidebar's own docking, splitting, and per-Session tab persistence apply unchanged.
The chat's code block is never hidden or replaced. Copying the source from the transcript, quoting i
t, or letting the model read it back still works, and a change to the chat's DOM costs the page its
input rather than the transcript.
## What it deliberately does not do
- It does not modify DeepSeek Harness. Everything it uses is a declared public extension point: `ctx

.sidebarRightTabs`, `sidebar.right.pane.tab`, and the `ctx.locale` / `ctx.slots` services.
- It does
not render inline in the transcript. Replacing a chat code block in place would need a rendering se
am that the product does not have, so the diagram lives in the Sidebar instead.
## How it finds diagrams
The chat renders an unknown language as a plain code card with no language attribute, so the page re
ads the first declaration line and accepts:

- `graph` / `flowchart` followed by a direction (`TB`, `TD`, `BT`, `RL`, `LR`);
- a known diagram ke
yword such as `sequenceDiagram`, `classDiagram`, `stateDiagram`, `erDiagram`, `gantt`, `pie`, `journ

ey`, `gitGraph`, `mindmap`, `timeline`, `xychart-beta`, `quadrantChart`, and the rest;
- leading bla
nk lines, `%%` comments, and a YAML front-matter block.
Mermaid's own parser is the final word: a source that fails to render shows the failure notice and i
ts source instead of a diagram.
## Viewing
The card is a fitted preview. A wheel over the card scrolls the page. The preview does not zoom or p
an, because that fought the page it sits in.
**Enlarge**, or a click on the diagram, opens the same diagram full screen. That view is a portal on
`document.body`, so the Sidebar's scroll container cannot clip it. It keeps no state once the card
nt.body`, so the Sidebar's scroll container cannot clip it. It keeps no state once the card is gone.
- The wheel zooms around the pointer. **−**, **+**, the percentage, **Fit**, and **Close** sit in th

e top bar.
- Dragging pans.
- `+` and `-` zoom from the center (`=` and `_` do the same). `0` fits t
he diagram to the window. `Esc` closes the view.
## Install
You need DeepSeek Harness and a profile whose Web GUI has the right Sidebar. The commands below use
the `web` profile. `package.json` sets `engines.dsh` to `*`; this repository does not name a minimum
profile. `package.json` sets `engines.dsh` to `*`; this repository does not name a minimum release.
Client plugins reach the page at load. After installing, hard-refresh the Web GUI. A host restart do
es not load a new client plugin into a page that is already open.

## Layout
| File | Role |

| `index.js` | Host half. Rendering is browser-only, so it contributes nothing. |
| `src/client.jsx`

| The page type, its body, and the scan. Built into `client.js`. |
| `src/diagram-source.mjs` | Whi

ch sources are diagrams, their keys, and whether a scan changed. |
| `src/viewport.mjs` | Fit ratio,

wheel factor, and zoom. |
| `src/render-policy.mjs` | Streaming keep rule and the one-at-a-time ren

der queue. |
